clue.text: Present tense used in log that's passed down

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: something used in another thing sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a diary is a daily log
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about which tense to use in a diary that has been handed down through a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits or titles are inherited, handed from parent to child.

clue.text: Killer's hot Italian mother beginning to network

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here taken from network

explanation.surface: A gangster film picture: an Italian mama connected to a criminal network.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired assassin is a contract killer.

clue.text: Regret being right about European writer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation for right goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for being correct about a European author.
explanation.walkthrough: RT is the abbreviation for right, rather than the more familiar R.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse for something done, a strong form of regret.

clue.text: Avoid smooth doctor and speak out, missing start of party game

parts.note: to duck is to avoid
to sand is to smooth a surface

indicators.note: out signals the letters of speak being put into disorder
the start of a word is its first letter, here from party

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a slick doctor and voice objections, while skipping the opening of a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SPEAK and 'missing' drops P (the start of party), leaving AKES. 'party game' looks like the definition, but party belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks and drakes is the pastime of skimming flat stones across water.

clue.text: Heads for France to cover area for confidential talk

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the French words enclose the letter for area

parts.note: tête is French for head; two heads give the word twice

explanation.surface: Instructions for two French leaders meeting privately over a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts the two TETEs around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête, literally head to head, is a private conversation between two people.

clue.text: Memento of priest found in church

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the priest goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic church
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A keepsake from a clergyman discovered inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of the past or of a saint, a keepsake.

clue.text: Hero may see nothing left after one day

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the earlier ones in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hero might see nobody remaining after just a day.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired and looked up to, a hero to fans.

clue.text: Instructive and accomplished performance in charge

parts.note: did means accomplished, carried out
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: An educational, polished show with someone in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to teach, so instructive in purpose.

clue.text: Generosity shown by the capital of Sweden, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the capital letter of the word Sweden is a large S, said as 'large ess'

explanation.surface: Is Stockholm known for its open-handedness, so people say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The capital of Sweden' looks like Stockholm, but it is the upper-case S that starts the word: a 'large S'.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, generosity.

clue.text: Questioned about suspicious rebel as seeing such a jacket

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the past-tense verb wraps the rearranged letters

parts.note: doubted means questioned, called into doubt

indicators.note: suspicious suggests something fishy, signalling the letters of rebel as being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone interrogated over a dodgy rebel's choice of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as seeing' links the wordplay to the definition 'such a jacket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-breasted jacket has overlapping front panels with two rows of buttons.

clue.text: Subject to snap

parts.note: a snap is a photo, informally a pic

explanation.surface: A subject liable to break suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject under discussion.

clue.text: Challenge from group of monks of high standing?

definitions.meaning: a demanding task that is hard to fulfil

definitions.text: group of monks of high standing?
definitions.meaning: a religious order whose members literally stand tall

explanation.surface: Is a test posed by a lofty monastery?
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is a demand that is difficult to meet; a religious order could whimsically be tall.

clue.text: Doctor means I must go before a complaint

indicators.note: these pieces come first and the single letter follows in the answer
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of means I are altered

explanation.surface: A physician says the speaker must leave before an ailment strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks medical but is the anagram signal; MEANS I rearranges to AMNESI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a medical condition or ailment.

clue.text: Cell walls of course keeping line by university writer

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the outer letters enclose the rest
the walls of a word are its outer letters, here from course
by means next to, so the line letter sits beside the others

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: Prison walls on a course hold a written line from a college writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls of' gives CE from course; 'keeping' puts UBICL inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small enclosed compartment, like a cell.

clue.text: Drugs could be a new philosophy of good taste

parts.note: aesthetics is the branch of philosophy concerned with beauty and taste

explanation.surface: Speculation that narcotics might be a fresh theory of beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaesthetics are drugs that remove sensation, used in surgery.

clue.text: Hamlet perhaps right — terrible loser with no heart

parts.note: a title is a legal right, as to property

indicators.note: terrible signals the remaining letters being shaken up
the heart of a word is its middle letter, which is taken out of loser

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict on a poor actor who is a heartless failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' drops S from LOSER; 'terrible' rearranges LOER into ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the lead part named in the play's title, an example of the role named.

clue.text: Added a couple of pages and finished

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages, two P's
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Someone put in two more sheets and then stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Appended means attached at the end, added on.

clue.text: Suggestion in favour of concession set up on a lake

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small concession to placate someone

explanation.surface: A plan backing a compromise arranged beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SOP into POS.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, a suggestion.

clue.text: Free trader even up, perhaps

indicators.note: to free something is to release it from its order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for free trade that might just even things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like a link, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic word meaning possibly or by chance.

clue.text: Betray trust, holding current allowance

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the phrase wraps the current symbol

parts.note: to rat on someone is to betray their trust
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A traitor keeps hold of a current allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside RATON.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies.

clue.text: Nice girls that are fetching?

parts.note: Nice is the French city, so French girls who are attractive, beautiful in French

explanation.surface: Well-behaved young women who look attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the French city, and the French word for beautiful women is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Belles are beautiful women, from the French for beautiful.

clue.text: Justify international being taken in by former scheme

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: being taken in means enclosed, so the international letter goes inside the scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Defending an international player duped by a past plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken in by' puts I inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain one's actions is to give reasons for them, to justify them.

clue.text: Creature from US city unfortunately docked

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: An animal from an American city, sadly with its tail cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' drops the S from ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope, an animal.

clue.text: Issue label returning with a note

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for label reads backwards

parts.note: a name is a label for something
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A batch of labels comes back accompanied by a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NAME into EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Criminal's sort of rail about reformed peers

indicators.note: about means around, so the rail word encloses the rearranged letters

parts.note: a dado rail is a moulding running along a wall

indicators.note: reformed means made over, so the letters of peers are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outlaw's railings surround a group of reformed noblemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a criminal of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: Most of journey with a learner will be an ordeal

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a journey
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A long drive with a learner driver is an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a testing experience, an ordeal to be endured.

clue.text: Transient lodger accommodating fool going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, backwards
accommodating means housing within, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: A temporary tenant takes in an idiot who then heads off west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' finds TLOD across 'Transient lodger'; 'going west' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: A Green's bid to change coats

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmental politician's attempt to alter clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Green's bid' looks like a Green Party bid for change; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdines are raincoats made of a tightly woven fabric of the same name.
